240	Right after, the matter of this segulah is mentioned
241	in the book of Devarim, chapter 7,	
242	Parashat Va'etchanan. Very interesting, note: "And you shall not intermarry with them."
243	This speaks here about the nations,
244	specifically; it speaks about the seven nations of Canaan, whom one must	
245	dispossess in order to inherit the land,
246	and drive them out, and not intermarry. Here we find the prohibition
247	of marriage with non-Jews: "You shall not give your daughter to his son, and his daughter you shall not take for your son." Why?
248	because... the key word. Why? "For he will turn your son away
249	from following Me."
250	from following Me.
251	"And they will serve other gods, and the anger of HaShem will be kindled against you, and He will destroy you quickly." That is,
252	your whole uniqueness is lost.
253	This will repeat itself again and again, and all
254	your uniqueness is in having received the Torah
255	and having accepted HaShem as God. Intermarriage with
256	foreigners will cause them to turn you away from following HaShem,
257	and then you will cease to be an Am Segulah. And you might say, you know, okay, let's not
258	be an Am Segulah, but let's be a nation like all the nations. No:
259	if we are not an Am Segulah, we will be destroyed. It is written here:
260	"and the anger of HaShem will be kindled against you, and He will destroy you quickly."
261	"For you are a holy people." Now, here again: "For you are a
262	holy people to HaShem your God."
263	"HaShem your God has chosen you to be for Him an Am Segulah out of all
264	the peoples that are on the face of the earth."
265	"Not because you were more numerous did HaShem desire you and choose you,
266	for you are the fewest of all peoples." That is, why
267	did the Holy One, blessed be He, choose us, choose us out of all
268	the peoples? Why did He choose us out of all the peoples?
269	If we were truly a great, strong, mighty people, one could
270	have said, perhaps. But no: we are the fewest of all
271	peoples. We were never,
272	ever numerous
273	in number.
274	And here, in fact, there is, I think, the primary distinction
275	between quality and quantity.
276	And there is a rule: this is the qualitative,
277	this is the quantity, and the rule
278	that is always true
279	is that
280	quality is always found in the minority
281	and not in the majority.
282	Always, for good and for bad, things are always
283	at the extremes; the middle is the average.
284	The extreme is always the more qualitative, positively or,
285	God forbid, negatively. So first of all He says: it is
286	not because you are more populous, more people.
287	"Not because you were more numerous than all the peoples did HaShem desire you and choose
288	you, for you are the fewest of all peoples." If so, why? "Because
289	of HaShem's love for you, and His keeping the oath that He swore
290	to your fathers, HaShem took you out with a mighty hand and
291	redeemed you from the house of bondage, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt." So this
292	began because of the oath to the Patriarchs.
293	So the choice of the Holy One, blessed be He, of us is because of
294	Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov; later on it is because He
295	offered us the Torah and we received the Torah,
296	and now He chose us out of all the peoples and gave us
297	His Torah.
298	So that is in chapter 7 of Devarim. In chapter 13:
299	"When you listen to the voice of HaShem your God, to keep all
300	His commandments that I command you this day, to do
301	what is right in the eyes of HaShem your God."
302	And now there is a commandment here that seems a bit
303	strange to us, but you will soon see how much depth it has:
304	"You are children of HaShem your God."
305	Not only are you the people, out of all those whom the Holy One, blessed be He,
306	created in the whole of creation, among all the peoples, He chose you
307	as a people, but now, as it were,
308	even more: you are children, as it were, of the Holy
309	One, blessed be He. "You are children of HaShem your God." And therefore,
310	"you shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness between your eyes
311	for the dead." And this is not understood: what, as it were? So what? Since
312	we are
313	children of HaShem our God, therefore, one needs to understand what
314	this is: "You shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness
315	between your eyes for the dead." Note,
316	this is a very great matter,
317	one must appreciate it as a topic in its own right, and this is the custom
318	of the nations of the world:
319	when someone dies, they do all kinds of acts of
320	self-flagellation, scratching, scratches, and
321	I don't know what, they harm themselves. They are in
322	terrible depression.
323	Of course, among us too, may HaShem protect, may it not happen to anyone,
324	there is a mitzvah to mourn for the dead, but it is forbidden
325	to reach a state of cutting oneself and making baldness, which is
326	all kinds of acts of self-flagellation.
327	Why? Because "you are children of HaShem your God." What
328	does this have to do with it? What does "you are children of HaShem
329	your God" have to do with the commandment not
330	to do extreme acts, God forbid, when a person of
331	Israel passes away, on the part of relatives, acquaintances and friends?
332	The secret of the matter is that since we are children
333	of HaShem our God,
334	HaShem Elokim is living and enduring forever, and all Israel have
335	a share in the World to Come.
336	And therefore,
337	among the nations of the world death is a totally
338	final station.
339	With us, death is not a totally final station; it is
340	a station along the way, after which comes the Resurrection of the dead,
341	and after that there is eternal existence, in eternal life.
342	So since, not only reincarnation, there is a possibility,
343	well, reincarnation is not a terribly positive thing,
344	because a soul comes to repair damages or to fulfill
345	a potential, whatever, I won't get into
346	the matter of reincarnation now, but that is not the point.
347	The point is that death is a separation of the soul from the
348	body; it is not a state of zeroing out and oblivion, and the body too
349	has hope, for it will rise in the Resurrection of the dead
350	and be rebuilt anew.
351	And in general, all Israel have a share in the World to Come,
352	and because "you are children of HaShem your God," one must
353	understand: one must grieve for the dead person who passed away, mainly
354	because we miss him. That is, the sorrow
355	is not so much for him but for us, that we miss
356	him. But one must know that we will meet again, with the help of
357	HaShem, all the people of Israel, in the Resurrection of the dead,
358	and in the reality of this eternity and holiness.
